findings.issue_text: Broken relative import in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts: '../oauth/decodeOAuthState' resolves to non-existent path after the file was moved, breaking the build for all consumers

minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to literal string '[ZodString]', making the schema semantically fabricated and causing safeParse to fail for every legitimate OAuth token response
refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token is never declared by either schema and the fallback assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the value, producing a bogus persisted key

CalendarService.ts (googlecalendar) persists the SafeParseReturnType wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of the parsed tokens, permanently breaking the Google credential after one refresh

refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a fetch Response in sharing mode but callers expect parsed token objects (e.g. res.data, expiresIn, tokenInfo.data), causing crashes or undefined token access in googlecalendar, hubspot, zoho-bigin, and zohocrm

Salesforce CalendarService.ts performs unconditional refresh before connection is constructed; existing credentials without refresh_token in key now send refresh_token=undefined, causing 400 errors and HttpError where jsforce's own refresh flow previously worked
Salesforce salesforceTokenSchema has no refresh_token field so refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token can be undefined when persisted
Salesforce CalendarService uses fragile check response.statusText !== 'OK' which fails with locale/proxy-dependent statusText (e.g. empty string on 200 from some proxies)
zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts passes credentialId where every other call site passes credential.userId, potentially a ReferenceError breaking Zoho Bigin if the variable is not in scope

app-credential.ts webhook header lookup uses raw env-driven header name which is case-sensitive against Node's lowercased headers, silently returning undefined and 403-ing all sync webhooks if misconfigured
app-credential.ts header value req.headers[...] can be string[], in which case strict !== comparison against the secret always fails

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts catchall keys like [z.string().toString()] are no-ops coercing to '[object Object]' instead of a real zod catchall, causing zod to strip all keys except access_token and lose refresh_token, scope, token_type from persisted credentials
parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts sets refresh_token to a placeholder string 'refresh_token' that doesn't exist in any schema, causing invalid-grant failures on next refresh

refreshOAuthTokens.ts shared-mode response is a raw fetch Response object but callers assume a parsed body shape, causing undefined tokens or garbage stored in shared mode (Google, Lark, HubSpot call sites)
zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing cross-user credential corruption via credential-sync endpoint
app-credential webhook has no HTTP method check and uses zod.parse instead of safeParse on req.body, causing 500s with stack traces on GET or malformed payloads with no rate limit
Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header) and no Content-Type, leaking third-party OAuth credentials to arbitrary callers

symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse of reqBody.keys in app-credential webhook are unguarded with no 32-byte key length verification, allowing malformed data to be written into credential.key without schema validation
No tests of any kind for the new shared modules (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, app-credential webhook)

Salesforce CalendarService refresh code bypasses refreshOAuthTokens() and never sources credentials from the sync endpoint even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set

parseRefreshTokenResponse discards the app-specific schema when sync is enabled, replacing it with minimumTokenResponseSchema computed with constant string keys that validate essentially nothing
Fabricated literal refresh_token ("refresh_token") is persisted when response lacks one, breaking subsequent refresh cycles; mutation executes in non-sync path too
Zoho-bigin callback URL changed from config-driven appConfig.slug to hardcoded 'zoho-bigin'
refreshOAuthTokens returns sync-mode response raw with no validation; callers expect provider-native response shapes and will misparse or crash

app-credential webhook has check-then-insert TOCTOU: findFirst then create with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), allowing duplicate credentials on concurrent deliveries; needs unique index + upsert or P2002 handling
In sync mode the caller-supplied app schema is discarded and replaced by the weaker minimum schema, so per-app invariants are not enforced and malformed sync responses are written to credential.key
office365calendar error logging removed; when safeParse fails, spreading false is a no-op so old expired credentials are written back and code continues as if refresh succeeded

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED flag is derived from two env vars but sync behavior also requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT checked inline in multiple places; webhook checks only the toggle, allowing credentials stored without refresh path consulting the sync endpoint

office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255-262: removed the error-handling branch that logged the zod error and MS response, replaced with a generic throw, losing provider failure details for debugging

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

app-credential.ts webhook header lookup uses raw env-driven header name which is case-sensitive against Node's lowercased headers, silently returning undefined and 403-ing all sync webhooks if misconfigured

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. In Node/Next.js, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase, and object property lookup is case-sensitive. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is configured with any uppercase characters (e.g., `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), the lookup will return `undefined`, causing the comparison to fail and the handler to 403 all webhook requests. The diff even notes the header name "should be in lowercase", but the code does not enforce/lowercase it, so this is a real misconfiguration-triggered defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts header value req.headers[...] can be string[], in which case strict !== comparison against the secret always fails

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check does `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next.js/Node, `req.headers[...]` is typed as `string | string[] | undefined` (IncomingHttpHeaders). If the header is provided multiple times, it can be a `string[]`, and a strict comparison against the env secret string will always fail, rejecting valid requests. The code does not normalize/handle the array case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts shared-mode response is a raw fetch Response object but callers assume a parsed body shape, causing undefined tokens or garbage stored in shared mode (Google, Lark, HubSpot call sites)

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns two different shapes depending on mode: in shared mode it returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response`, while in non-shared mode it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (often an SDK object). Several call sites assume the non-shared return type. Example: `GoogleCalendarService` does `const token = res?.data;` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens`; a `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `googleCredentials.access_token/expiry_date` become `undefined` (and then `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` will fail/throw in shared mode). `HubspotCalendarService` assigns the result to `HubspotToken`, but in shared mode it will be a `Response`, not a token object. `LarkCalendarService` passes the result to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)` which expects the Lark refresh-token JSON shape, but in shared mode it will be the credential-sync endpoint response (per comment: “only contain the access token and expiry date”), so parsing/logic will break. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing cross-user credential corruption via credential-sync endpoint
app-credential webhook has no HTTP method check and uses zod.parse instead of safeParse on req.body, causing 500s with stack traces on GET or malformed payloads with no rate limit
Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header) and no Content-Type, leaking third-party OAuth credentials to arbitrary callers

adjudication.rationale: In `refreshOAuthTokens`, the POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` indeed does not add any custom authentication header (it only sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in a `URLSearchParams` body). However, the proposed finding’s core claim about “leaking third-party OAuth credentials to arbitrary callers” is not supported by the diff: no OAuth credentials/tokens are sent in this request. Also, the “no Content-Type” part is not clearly true because `fetch` with a `URLSearchParams` body typically sets `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8` automatically. Finally, there is no indication in the diff that this endpoint is supposed to use `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (that secret is used for the *incoming* webhook handler), and the code comments explicitly say to customize the payload per endpoint requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse of reqBody.keys in app-credential webhook are unguarded with no 32-byte key length verification, allowing malformed data to be written into credential.key without schema validation

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts and parses user-supplied `reqBody.keys` via `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` with no try/catch and no validation of the decrypted structure before persisting it (`data: { key: keys }`). If decryption fails or the decrypted string is not valid JSON, `JSON.parse` will throw and the route will error (500). Additionally, even if parsing succeeds, any JSON shape can be written into `credential.key` because there is no schema validation here. The code also defaults the encryption key to an empty string (`process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`), and there is no explicit 32-byte/AES-256 key-length check in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse discards the app-specific schema when sync is enabled, replacing it with minimumTokenResponseSchema computed with constant string keys that validate essentially nothing

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, it ignores the caller-provided `schema` and instead uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema`.

That “minimum” schema is effectively broken/meaningless as written: it tries to model “any numeric expiry field” via computed object keys (`[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: ...`), but those keys evaluate to a single constant string at runtime (e.g. `"[object Object]"`), so it does *not* validate arbitrary token fields/expiry fields. Also, since it’s a plain `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`, it won’t actually accept/retain arbitrary extra properties as the comments claim.

So when sync is enabled, app-specific token response validation is discarded and replaced with a schema that largely doesn’t enforce the intended structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns sync-mode response raw with no validation; callers expect provider-native response shapes and will misparse or crash

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object in “sync mode” (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`). But several callers still assume the *non-sync* provider-native return shape. Example: in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assigns `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data;` and reads `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and the code will misparse/crash. Similarly, HubSpot assigns the result to `HubspotToken`, which will also be wrong in sync mode. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and is verifiable from the code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed key [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to literal string "[object Object]" instead of a catch-all, so every real OAuth token response fails the parse and credential-sharing mode throws for every app

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts persists the full SafeParseResult wrapper object ({success, data, ...}) into credential.key JSON column, corrupting the credential shape permanently

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the full Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not `refreshTokenResponse.data`. That means the JSON column `credential.key` would store the wrapper object instead of the expected credential shape, corrupting the stored credential format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When token response has no refresh_token, the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" is written into the credential and later sent to providers as the refresh token, permanently poisoning the credential

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly mutates parsed token data: if `refresh_token` is missing it sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, so the literal string can be written into the stored credential. While in the "credential sync" mode the refresh flow may not use the provider refresh token (it calls `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), this does still poison persisted data and can later be used as a refresh token if sync is disabled/misconfigured or other code paths rely on the stored refresh token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook has check-then-insert TOCTOU: findFirst then create with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), allowing duplicate credentials on concurrent deliveries; needs unique index + upsert or P2002 handling

adjudication.rationale: In the new `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler, the code does a separate `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }})` and then conditionally `create(...)` if none is found. This is a classic check-then-act race: two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no row” and both attempt `create`. If there is no DB uniqueness constraint, this can create duplicate credentials; if there is a unique constraint, the second `create` will throw (e.g., Prisma P2002) and the handler doesn’t catch it, causing a 500. The diff does not add any transaction/upsert/P2002 handling to make this atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In sync mode the caller-supplied app schema is discarded and replaced by the weaker minimum schema, so per-app invariants are not enforced and malformed sync responses are written to credential.key

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the function ignores the caller-provided `schema` and instead validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (`minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)`), which is strictly weaker than per-app schemas. It also force-injects a `refresh_token` placeholder if missing. Call sites then persist the parsed result into credentials (e.g., `Office365CalendarService` merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates `prisma.credential`), so in sync mode malformed/partial token payloads that would fail the app-specific schema can still be accepted and written to `credential.key`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar error logging removed; when safeParse fails, spreading false is a no-op so old expired credentials are written back and code continues as if refresh succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In `Office365CalendarService`, the diff replaces `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` plus conditional `console.error` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. That helper explicitly `throw`s when `.safeParse` is not successful, so the code will not proceed to spread a failing parse result or write “old expired credentials” back in the failure case. Also, `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` only becomes a no-op spread when `success` is false, which cannot happen after `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns. The removal of logging is real, but the claimed behavior (continuing on failed safeParse and persisting stale creds as if refresh succeeded) is not introduced by this diff and is prevented by the new helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook lacks HTTP method guard and uses z.parse instead of safeParse, so GET or malformed body throws unhandled ZodError → 500 instead of 400

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED flag is derived from two env vars but sync behavior also requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT checked inline in multiple places; webhook checks only the toggle, allowing credentials stored without refresh path consulting the sync endpoint

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is used as a feature gate, while `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is additionally checked in `refreshOAuthTokens` / `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to decide whether to delegate refresh to an external endpoint. The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) only checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (and the webhook secret), and does not consult `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`—but the diff does not establish that the webhook must be disabled when the sync endpoint is unset, nor that `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is “derived from two env vars”. Also, “allowing credentials stored without refresh path consulting the sync endpoint” is just the designed branching: refresh consults the sync endpoint only when it exists. Whether that is incorrect depends on intent not proven by the diff. Therefore the finding is not a verifiable defect from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10: broken Zod schema — z.string().toString() evaluates to literal 'ZodString', so the 'permissive' schema is actually { access_token: string, ZodString: number } and doesn't validate anything

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed keys use `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()`. In JavaScript/TypeScript object literals, computed property names must evaluate to an actual string key at definition time, so these expressions produce a single literal key (typically something like "ZodString" / "ZodOptional" or "[object Object]"), not a wildcard for “any string key”. As a result, the schema becomes something like `{ access_token: string, "ZodString": number, "ZodOptional": unknown? }`, which will not match real token responses (e.g., `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, etc.) and will cause `safeParse` to fail and throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` when the feature flag path is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:23-25: fabricated refresh_token placeholder 'refresh_token' overwrites the real refresh token in office365 CalendarService and is persisted via prisma.credential.update, permanently destroying the user's credential (data loss)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after a successful `safeParse`, it forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the provider response lacks a refresh token. In `Office365CalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`. If Microsoft’s refresh response omits `refresh_token` (common), the placeholder string overwrites the existing real `o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token`, and the updated credentials are persisted with `prisma.credential.update`, causing loss of the real refresh token and breaking future refreshes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255-262: removed the error-handling branch that logged the zod error and MS response, replaced with a generic throw, losing provider failure details for debugging

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decrypted keys blob stored to DB without any schema validation in app-credential.ts webhook

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` and immediately `JSON.parse`s it, then writes the resulting `keys` object directly into `prisma.credential.update/create({ data: { key: keys, ... } })`. There is no validation step (e.g., a zod schema per `appSlug`/`appMetadata.type`) to ensure the decrypted blob has the expected shape or fields for that app before persisting it. Since the webhook body is externally supplied (only guarded by a shared secret header), malformed or unexpected key structures can be stored and later break consumers expecting a specific credential schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single global static webhook secret with no per-user scoping allows overwriting any user's credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes requests solely by checking a single shared secret in a header (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). After that, it trusts the `userId` from the request body and performs `prisma.credential.update/create` for that `userId` and `appSlug` without any additional per-user scoping, signature, or authorization. Therefore, any caller who knows/leaks the global webhook secret can submit a payload with an arbitrary `userId` and overwrite/create credentials for any user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-timing-safe string comparison for webhook secret authorization

adjudication.rationale:
In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook authorization check compares the provided secret to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using a normal JS `!==` string comparison:

```ts
if (req.headers[... ] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) { ... }
```

This is not a constant-time comparison, so it can theoretically leak information via timing differences when an attacker probes the endpoint with varying prefixes of the secret. A timing-safe comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on fixed-length buffers) would avoid that class of side-channel.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No nonce/replay protection on webhook endpoint

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler at `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authenticates requests solely by comparing a static shared secret in a header (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). There is no timestamp, nonce, signature/HMAC over the body, or request ID storage to detect duplicates or out-of-order delivery. As a result, any previously observed valid request can be replayed indefinitely, potentially re-applying old credentials (e.g., overwriting newer keys if an older payload is replayed later). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Literal string "refresh_token" written into credential record when sync endpoint omits refresh_token, permanently breaking integration on next refresh
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys produce literal key "z.string()", rejecting every valid token response in credential-sharing mode

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed property names inside `z.object({ ... })`:
```ts
[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),
[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),
```
In JS/TS object literals, computed keys are evaluated immediately to a *single string* (the result of `toString()` on the Zod schema object), producing a literal property name (e.g. `"[object Object]"`), not an index signature / “any key”. Zod’s `z.object` also doesn’t treat such entries as catch-all rules for arbitrary keys. Therefore `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will require that exact bizarre key to exist, and typical OAuth token responses (with keys like `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, etc.) will fail validation in credential-sharing mode.

So the finding describes a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod SafeParseResult wrapper object stored as user's credential key instead of parsed data, destroying Google credentials on first refresh

However, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed `data` itself. This means the DB credential `key` will store the wrapper object instead of the credential payload, whereas previously it stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the parsed data). This will change the shape of stored credentials and can break subsequent code that expects `credential.key` to be the credential fields directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sync endpoint fetch response returned without validation, allowing compromised/MITM endpoint to inject arbitrary access tokens
Sync endpoint URL has no scheme enforcement (http:// accepted) and no TLS or response signing

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and uses it directly in `refreshOAuthTokens`:

```ts
const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { ... })
```

There is no validation that the URL is `https://` (or otherwise enforces TLS), so an `http://` endpoint would be accepted if configured, allowing cleartext transport/MITM risk. adjudication_records.issue_text: New logic in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, app-credential.ts webhook endpoint, and rewired refresh paths across ~10 services has zero accompanying tests

adjudication_records.issue_text: The minimum schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts is a no-op validator: computed keys [z.string().toString()] evaluate to the literal string "" as the object key, collapsing into duplicate "" keys so the schema can never validate what its author intended
When credential-sharing is enabled, all app-specific validation is discarded: any object containing a string access_token passes validation
refresh_token is defaulted to the sentinel string "refresh_token" which is persisted to prisma.credential and will silently break future refreshes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly mutates the parsed token payload: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow does `const tokenResponse = parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema);` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) before persisting back to Prisma via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: o365AuthCredentials } })`. Since many OAuth providers do not return `refresh_token` on refresh, this change can overwrite a previously valid stored refresh token with the sentinel string "refresh_token", causing subsequent refresh attempts to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook uses z.parse without a try/catch or error handler, causing unhandled rejection (500 with stack exposure) on invalid bodies

adjudication_records.issue_text: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) in app-credential.ts can throw on any malformed ciphertext, and none of the three failure branches (bad body, bad key, missing user) have tests

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no try/catch. If `reqBody.keys` is malformed, the encryption key is wrong/empty, `symmetricDecrypt` throws/returns non-JSON, or `JSON.parse` fails, the request will error out with an unhandled exception (500) rather than a controlled 4xx response—this is a real correctness/robustness issue introduced by the diff. However, the claim that "none of the ... failure branches have tests" is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone (it only shows no tests were added here, not that no tests exist elsewhere).

Google CalendarService.ts sharing-enabled path reads '.data' off a raw fetch Response (which is undefined), causing token.access_token to throw TypeError on the first calendar operation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. In the sharing-enabled branch, `refreshOAuthTokens` calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. A Fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property (it requires `await res.json()` / `await res.text()`), so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw a `TypeError` when that path is exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook writes JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) output verbatim to credential.key with no shape validation, potentially overwriting a working credential with unusable data and no backup or rollback

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts `reqBody.keys`, immediately `JSON.parse(...)`s it, and then writes the resulting value directly into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` / `create({ data: { key: keys, ... } })` without any validation of the decrypted JSON’s expected shape for the given `appSlug`/`appMetadata.type`. Since `credential.key` is typically a JSON field, Prisma will accept many JSON shapes, so a malformed-but-parseable payload can overwrite an existing working credential with unusable data, with no rollback/backup logic in this endpoint.
